stage_2_story.text_en:
Last spring, Avi noticed that his beloved garden was in serious trouble. The tomato plants had developed a strange white fungus on their leaves, and tiny insects were eating holes in the pepper plants. To make matters worse, after every rainstorm, water would pool around the vegetable beds because the drainage was completely blocked by roots and old soil.

Avi decided to tackle the problems one at a time. First, he dug narrow channels around the garden beds to improve the drainage so that rainwater could flow away properly. Then he mixed a natural pesticide from neem oil and sprayed it carefully on the affected plants to drive away the insects without harming the soil.

For the fungus problem, Avi removed all the infected leaves through careful pruning and disposed of them far from the garden. He also pulled out every weed that had grown between the rows, since weeds steal nutrients from the healthy plants.

Next, Avi visited the local nursery and bought several bags of fertilizer and a large bale of mulch. He spread the fertilizer evenly across the beds to give the weakened plants a boost of nutrition. Then he laid a thick layer of mulch around the base of each plant to keep the soil moist and prevent new weeds from sprouting.

Avi also decided to transplant some of the crowded seedlings into a new raised bed he had built over the weekend. Finally, he gave the overgrown hedges along the garden path a thorough trimming so that more sunlight could reach the vegetables. As autumn arrived, he collected all the garden waste — dead leaves, plant stems, and vegetable scraps — and added them to his compost bin. By the following spring, Avi's garden was healthier and more productive than ever before.
